headline: High: shared workspace writes and vendor-hosted Q&A create default risks of data leakage and cascading errors; prompt injection is lower but present via shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes marketing files and builds on shared context; Agent B is a RAG-style Q&A system over workspace pages. If A’s content is later ingested by B, attacker-controlled text can steer B’s responses. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a-authored content is imported into agent_b's workspace pages or prompts, injection becomes actionable.
IF agent_b treats workspace text as instruction-like content without provenance checks, malicious phrasing can steer outputs.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to A-generated content before B ingests it.
Require B to quote-and-cite source passages instead of following instructions in content.
Restrict A from writing directly into pages B summarizes.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read and write filesystem content and call APIs; Agent B can access pages and databases in the user’s workspace and sends data to Notion vendor backends. If the same workspace contains sensitive material, B can transmit it to third-party inference, while A can also persist or reshape it. The shared workspace path makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are available to agent_b, those contents may be sent to vendor backends.
IF agent_a writes derived marketing context into shared files, agent_b can later ingest and expose it in answers.
mitigations: Move sensitive pages out of the shared workspace.
Limit B to a non-sensitive subspace or test workspace.
Disable A writes to any directory B can read.
Review Notion workspace sharing and access scopes.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data partitioning and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has filesystem write and subprocess capability, while Agent B has shared workspace state across instances but no host execution or filesystem write. They do not both have unrestricted write to the same OS directory, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping mutation of shared workspace content can cause conflicts and stale overwrites.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace artifact, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF A writes files that B mirrors into workspace pages, concurrent updates can diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate edit targets for A and B.
Use timestamps or version fields on shared artifacts.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Export B outputs before A rewrites source files.
requires-engineering: add locking or merge resolution for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is explicitly a workspace Q&A system grounded in content, so it can treat A’s generated marketing material as authoritative input. A can produce persuasive but unverified claims, and B can then summarize or operationalize them without a built-in verification step. That creates a default pathway for propagating errors into downstream work products.
conditions: IF A-generated claims are placed into pages B uses for grounding, B may repeat them as facts.
IF B is used to draft customer-facing or internal docs from A output, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B ingests them.
Mark A-generated text as untrusted draft content.
Ask B to surface source excerpts alongside summaries.
Limit B to retrieval, not action-taking, for A-authored pages.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends, while Agent A is an open-source marketing skill with filesystem and API access. If regulated or sensitive content is placed in the workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific regulated data class, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Notion workspace, vendor-hosted processing may violate local policy.
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between A-written files and B-hosted pages, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm retention settings for Notion pages used by B.
Document which data classes A may write.
Review workspace access and deletion workflows.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
